purpose: Produce a coherent private first draft that specifies the TDRG protocol/evaluation contract and sharply separates verified v0.1 implementation evidence from the TM-01--TM-18 roadmap.
audience: Researchers in scholarly communication, peer-review governance, network trust, privacy, research software, and reproducibility; protocol implementers and scientific reviewers.
outline: Privacy, interoperability, reproducibility, and stop rules
bibliography_inputs: primary-source pages and papers named in claim-ledger.json
human_questions: Who will own normative protocol authorship and independent security review?
Which venue and article type determine the final length and formatting?
What frozen statistical precision, subgroup-harm, and privacy thresholds should govern TM-18?
Which license and archival identifier are authorized for paper and tooling releases?
constraints: Private draft; no submission, publication, or external contact.
Current implementation evidence is limited to revision 9da0cd4 and the 11 locally rerun tests.
Every implemented subtest is reported below the TM-row level.
Official standards pages are treated as web standards sources, not as indexed journal articles.
Retrieval capability: web primary-source retrieval plus local evidence packets; no specialized research corpus was available.
excluded_claims: Novel invention of decentralized peer review, graph routing, local trust, anonymous reputation, fair assignment, or immutable review records.
Cryptographic signatures, identity uniqueness, Sybil resistance, collusion resistance, anonymity, unlinkability, appeals/opening, or fork reconciliation in v0.1.
A0--A4 comparative benefit, attack resistance, field efficacy, reviewer competence, or scientific validity.
Complete JSON Schema conformance or cross-platform byte-identical replay.
